properties.name: MUSHROOM ROCK DAY USE AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Mushroom Rock Day Use Area is located off Rock Creek Road in McCreary County. This is a small day use site with limited development near Rock Creek. There is a parking area, crushed gravel path and limited visitor information.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From Whitley City, take US 27 south for 4.7 miles. Turn right onto KY 92 at the traffic light. Travel 6.3 miles then turn left onto KY 1363 and continue for 4.6 miles. Turn left at White Oak Junction Church and continue for 1 mile. The site is on your right.

properties.name: LONGBOW MARINA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Longbow Marina is located on Cave Run Lake near Longbow Boat Ramp. The Marina has boat slips for rent and full-service gasoline pumps.
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 and go south on KY 801. Continue on 801, which merges into KY 1274. Follow 1274 for several miles. Turn right onto Longbow Road.

properties.name: TURKEY FOOT CAMPGROUND
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Turkey Foot Campground is located off Elsam Fork Road (Forest #345) along the banks of War Fork Creek in Jackson County. The gravel road into the campground is steep. There is a low water ford across the creek at the campground entrance. Each of the 15 primitive, first come, first served sites are equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, tent pad and lantern pole. There is no water, electricity or dump station available in the campground. A playfield with a horseshoe pit is located at the end of camping area alongside the creek. The area serves as a trailhead for the Turkey Foot Loop Trail system.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions:
From US 421: take KY 587 north and turn left onto Forest Road 4 (Turkey Foot Road). Follow FR 4 to FR 345 (Elsam Fork Road). Turn right onto 345 and follow signs to the campground. From Arvel take KY 587 south and turn right onto Forest Road 4 (Turkey Foot Road). Follow FR 4 to FR 345 (Elsam Fork Road). Turn right onto 345 and follow signs to the campground.

From Berea: From I-75, take Berea Exit 76. Head east on KY 21. Stay on KY 21E (Big Hill Road) approximately 5 miles until it ends at US 421. Turn right (south) on US 421. Take US 421 west for approximately 18.4 miles to McKee, KY. Turn left onto KY 89. Travel approximately 3 miles on KY 89N and turn right on Macedonia Road for 0.5-mile. Turn left on Forest Service Road #4 (Turkey Foot Road) for 1 mile. The road turns to gravel. After 1.9 miles, turn left onto Forest Service Road 345 (Elsam Fork Road) and follow signs to the campground.

properties.name: TWIN KNOBS RECREATION AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
Twin Knobs Recreation Area is a 700-acre facility located off KY 801 on the north shore of Cave Run Lake. This family-friendly recreation area includes a large campground with tent and RV sites, three group use areas, bath houses with showers, scenic foot trails with overlooks, and nearby boat ramps with vehicle and boat trailer parking. A sandy beach with a roped swimming area offers visitors a spectacular view of the lake. Volleyball courts, basketball hoops and horseshoe pits provide local entertainment. RV sites range from electric-only to full hookups. There is an RV dump station. A campground store with ice, firewood, camping gear and food is on-site.
The three group use areas are reservable: East (capacity up to 100 persons), West (capacity up to 180 persons), and Tent Area (capacity up to 60 persons).
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $35 per night
Premium Single Site: $45 per night
Double Site: $50 per night
Premium Double Site: $64 per night
Electric hook-up Fee: $13 per night
Electric and water hook-up Fee: $20 per night
Electric, water and sewer hook-up Fee: $25 per night
Additional Vehicle Fee: $10 per vehicle per night
Dump Station Fee: $10 per use.
details.hours:
Check-in: 2 p.m.
Checkout: 11:00 a.m.
Only registered campers are allowed at Twin Knobs after 10 p.m.
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. The campground is 9 miles on the right.

details.description: Windy Bay Fishing Site is located off KY 801 on the shores of Cave Run Lake. Windy Bay Trails #1223/A/B make two short connected loops of the area. The site has designated parking and trash collection.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Day use only: open 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. Proceed about 12 miles and turn right on Forest Service Road 1179.

properties.name: BEE ROCK BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Bee Rock Boat Ramp is located within the Bee Rock Recreation Area and provides access to the Rockcastle River. Upstream, the 15.9-mile segment of Rockcastle River from KY 1956 (old Highway 80) bridge to the backwaters of Lake Cumberland near Bee Rock is designated a Kentucky Wild River and includes one of the most challenging whitewater runs in Kentucky. It is a long stretch of water with several Class III and at least one Class IV rapid along the way. It should be attempted only by experienced, well-equipped paddlers. Plan on at least 8 hours for the trip. The take-out is at the Bee Rock Boat Ramp. Downstream, the last section of the Rockcastle River begins at Bee Rock Boat Ramp and ends at the Rockcastle Boat Ramp at the mouth of the river. Lake Cumberland inundates most of this section of the Rockcastle and this 7-mile flat water float is perfect for beginners and families. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The site has parking, signage, trash collection and security lighting. The boat ramp has parking and visitor information.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
$5 per day per vehicle
$7 per three day
$50 annual
details.directions: From I-75, take exit 38 (London). Travel west on KY 192 for 18 miles to the Rockcastle River. After crossing River, turn right onto Forest Service Road 623.

properties.name: TWENTY SIX BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Twenty Six Boat Ramp provides access to the Licking River as it flows into Cave Run Lake. Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species. Cave Run Lake is well-known for excellent muskie fishing. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The site includes parking.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. At the intersection of KY 801 and KY 1274, stay on 801 and turn right onto KY 519. After several miles, turn right onto KY 772. Turn right onto County Road 1474. The boat ramp is on the right. From West Liberty, follow KY 7 north for 5.4 mi. Turn left onto KY 772, go 3.1 miles. Turn right onto County Road 1474 and go .4 miles to ramp.

properties.name: LONG BEND FISHING SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Long Bend Fishing Site is a popular fishing area located off of Forest Service Road 611A near Laurel River Dam. Fishing for black bass, rainbow trout, walleye, crappie, blue gill and catfish is excellent.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From I-75, at London Exit 38, turn west on KY 192, go 14.2 miles, then turn south (left) on KY 1193, go 3 miles. Turn onto Forest Road 611A and follow to parking area.

properties.name: CHIMNEY TOP OVERLOOK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Chimney Top Overlook is located at the end of Chimney Top Road (Forest #10) and provides access to Chimney Top Trail #235 and Princess Arch Trail #233. The overlook towers 400 feet above the Red River and provides sweeping views of the Red River Gorge. Nearby Princess Arch is a beautiful slender arch that visitors can walk over and under. The site has designated parking, visitor information, trash collection and picnic tables.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions:
Traveling east on the Mountain Parkway, take exit 33 at Slade. Turn left and then right onto KY 15. Travel east 7 miles to KY 715 on the left. Turn left onto 715 and continue 2.1 miles to Chimney Top Road on the left. Follow Chimney Top Road 4.5 miles to its terminus.
From exit 40, head west on KY 15 and turn right on KY 715. Continue 2.1 miles to Chimney Top Road on the left. Follow Chimney Top Road 4.5 miles to its terminus.

properties.name: LAUREL BRIDGE BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Laurel Bridge Boat Ramp is located near Laurel Bridge Picnic Area and provides access to the upper arm of Laurel River Lake. Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species including black bass, rainbow trout, walleye, crappie, blue gill, and catfish. Night fishing for trout is also popular during the summer months. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The site has visitor information and nearby parking in the lot above the boat ramp.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
$5 per day per vehicle
$7 per three day
$50 annual
details.directions: From I-75 exit 29 (Corbin), take KY 770 west for 1.3 miles. Turn left on KY 312 for 0.6-mile. Turn left into the recreation area.

Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species. Cave Run Lake is well-known for excellent muskie fishing. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The site includes parking, signage, trash collection, security lighting and a courtesy dock.
details.feeDescription:

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Lick Creek Trailhead is located off Forest Road 622 just outside Whitley City and provides access to Lick Creek Falls and Princess Falls via Lick Creek Trail #631 and Lick Creek Falls Trail #631A. Lick Creek Trail ends at Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail (#100). The site has parking and visitor information.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: At Whitley City take KY 478 west to KY 1651. Turn left (south) and follow 1651 for 1 mile before reaching Forest Service Road 622 on your right (the first paved road past the school bus garage). The trailhead is 100 feet up Forest Service Road 622 on your left at the gate.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Shallow Flats Wildlife Viewing Area is located off of KY 801 overlooking a wetland adjacent to Cave Run Lake. The area provides excellent opportunities to view waterfowl from an accessible observation deck or along Shallow Flats Trail #1209 and Shallow Pond Trail #1211.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. Continue 8.6 miles to the Shallow Flats Wildlife Viewing Area. From Farmers, take US 60 for 5.3 miles.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Keno Shooting Range is located off Worley Road (Forest #5099) just south of Keno Road (#750) in Pulaski County. properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Holly Bay Recreation Area is located on the west side of Laurel River Lake and offers a variety of family-friendly recreation opportunities. The area includes a developed campground with wooded campsites near the lakeshore, a bathhouse with showers, a boat ramp, a fish cleaning station and easy access to Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail #100 and Wintergreen Trail #480. The 75 drive-in campsites are reservable and have electricity, water, a paved vehicle pad, gravel tent pad, fire ring, picnic table and lantern pole. The 19 walk-in tent campsites are on a first-come, first-served basis and have access to centrally located water, but no electricity. These primitive sites have a gravel tent pad, fire ring, picnic table, lantern pole and bear-resistant food storage lockers. The area is adjacent to Holly Bay Marina, a full-service marina where visitors may rent boats and purchase fuel, groceries, and other supplies. Nearby Spillway Beach, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, provides public swimming access to the lake.

properties.name: BIG BRANCH CANOE LAUNCH
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Big Branch Canoe Launch is located along Sandfield Road off KY 746 and provides access to the upper "wild" section of the Red Wild and Scenic River. In 1993, a 19.4-mile segment of the Red River, stretching from KY 746 to the ford below Schoolhouse Branch, was designated a National Wild and Scenic River. The Upper Red River is a 10.8-mile section that is considered one of the most challenging stretches of whitewater in the southeastern United States. Beginning at the Big Branch Canoe Launch, the river twists through a series of Class III rapids. During high water, this section is very dangerous. Due to the remote location within the Clifty Wilderness, rescues and walk-outs are exceedingly difficult. The Upper Red River should only be attempted by expert paddlers. The entire run takes about 6 hours. The site has parking, visitor information and steps to the launch.

details.hours: Day use only: open 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

Turn right and follow 746 north past the bridge over the Red River to KY 3357 (Sandfield Road) on the right.  Look for a signed right turn onto a gravel road for the Big Branch river access. details.description: Clear Creek Boat Ramp is located off Clear Creek Road (#129) near the start of Zilpo Scenic Byway. A variety of wildlife, including rare birds, calls this location home year-round. Clear Creek Lake area provides access to Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail #100, as well as a small and tranquil picnic area, parking area and campground. Like the rest of the byway, fall is a particularly good time to visit Clear Creek Lake, as it is a popular migration stop for ducks and geese. Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species. The 40-acre lake is stocked with bluegill, bass, and catfish and is open to non-gas powered motorized vessels. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The nearby Scott Creek Marina is a full-service marina where boaters may purchase fuel, groceries and other supplies.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: S-Tree Campground sits on a ridge above Horse Lick Creek near McKee in Jackson County, Kentucky. Each of the 20 first-come, first-served campsites has a picnic table, tent pad, fire ring and lantern pole. The campground's small first come, first served picnic area features a historic shelter that was constructed in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps. The campground is popular with off-highway vehicle (OHV) enthusiasts due to its proximity to Renfro Loop OHV Trail #302. The campground cannot accommodate trailers longer than 25 feet due to one lane roads and no turn-outs.

details.description: Bee Rock Campground is located off KY 192 within the Bee Rock Recreation Area along the banks of the Rockcastle River and features 25 wooded, first-come, first-served campsites with scenic views of rocks, cliffs, and the Rockcastle River. The campground features Old Sublimity Bridge, a historic structure built by the Civilian Conservation Corps that has been restored for foot travel only. The campground features sites for both small RVs and tents. Each site has a fire ring and lantern post with access to many shared picnic tables. Bee Rock Boat Ramp is located within the campground on the Laurel County side. From the campground, visitors can access Rockcastle Connector Trail #401A, Rockcastle Narrows Trail #503 and Bee Rock Loop Trail #529.

The area can comfortably support 110 visitors spread across the 16 individual picnic sites. Each site has its own grill and picnic table. Two nearby fields are suitable for playing ball or other outdoor activities. There are no developed trails, but the area has lots of room to explore. Site amenities include parking, visitor information, grills and picnic tables.

Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail #100, Clear Creek Lake Trail #103 and Buck Creek Trail #118 are accessible from this area and connect to over 50 miles of trails. Nearby Clear Creek is generally shallow but can run swiftly during rainy seasons. Campsites include tent or RV pads, picnic tables, fire rings and lantern poles. There is no electricity or shower facilities.

properties.name: MOUTH OF LAUREL BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Mouth of Laurel Boat Ramp is located at the confluence of Laurel River and Lake Cumberland. Downstream, small motorized boats can access Lake Cumberland. Upstream, the Cumberland River flows 11.6 miles from the base of the Cumberland Falls to the Mouth of Laurel. This section is one of the few whitewater runs that can be made year-round. It is rated as a Class III with several difficult rapids that should be attempted only by intermediate and advanced paddlers. The last several miles are flat water as the river flows into upper reaches of Lake Cumberland. Plan on 4-6 hours for the trip from the Falls to this boat ramp. The site has parking and visitor information.

From 1881 to 1935, the area was the site of a coal mining town operated by the Barren Fork Mining and Coal Company. Today, the campground offers 41 campsites that accommodate horse trailers and RVs up to 35 feet. A picnic shelter at the campground is available for group-use. Several interconnecting trails provide miles of riding pleasure. A nearby pond has water for horses. Visitors can also enjoy fishing at a nearby pond.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The historic Tater Knob Fire Tower in Bath County was originally constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps and later updated in 1964. It was closed to the public after an arson fire destroyed the structure on December 3, 2008. The fire burned all of the supporting wood frame of the lookout cab underneath its metal exterior. The tower is no longer safe for visitors. The stairs leading to the deck and Tater Knob Fire Tower itself are closed to all public entry.

properties.name: BLACKWATER BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Blackwater Boat Ramp is located on Cave Run Lake among the beautiful mountains of eastern Kentucky. Built for flood protection by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this 8,270 lake provides flood protection to the lower Licking River valley, supplies water to area communities, improves water flow conditions on the Licking River, and offers habitat for many species of fish and wildlife. Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species. Cave Run Lake is well-known for excellent muskie fishing. Cave Run Lake is popular with swimmers, but swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launching ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Grove Boat-In Campground is one of two boat-in campgrounds on Laurel River Lake. The campground has 22 first come, first served campsites, most of which are located near the water's edge with boat moorings available. details.description: Grove Drive-In Campground is perched on a forested ridge above Laurel River Lake in Kentucky's Daniel Boone National Forest. The lake, fed by the Laurel River, is considered one of the most scenic lakes in the state. Boating, fishing, hiking and biking are greatly enjoyed by campers. Grove Campground is located off Grove Road (#558) on a forested ridge above Laurel River Lake near Grove Boat Ramp and Marina. Of the 40 drive-in sites, Loop B is reservable, and Loop A is first come, first served. Thirty-five drive-in sites have electricity and water and five have water only. All drive-in sites have a paved vehicle pad, gravel tent pad, fire ring, picnic table and lantern pole. The four walk-in tent sites are first come, first served and have access to water, but no electricity. These primitive sites have a gravel tent pad, fire ring, picnic table, lantern pole and bear-proof food storage lockers. Several short trails start in the campground including  Duff Branch Trail #440, Spruce Creek Trail #441, Fishing Point Trail (#442), Singing Hills Trail #443 and Oak Branch Trail #444.

properties.name: FITCHBURG FURNACE INTERPRETIVE SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Fitchburg Furnace was constructed in 1868 and operated at the peak of the iron industry. In 1870, with 250 men, Fitchburg produced 900 tons of pig iron. Its venture was cut short in 1875. Its intricate architectural design places it among the top 25 dry-stone masonry structures worldwide and portions of the furnace remain standing to this day. At 81 feet tall, the dual-stack furnace is considered the largest charcoal iron furnace in the world and was the last of such furnaces to be built in America. The interpretive site is located off Fitchburg Road (KY 975) in Estill County and provides designated parking, visitor information, picnic tables and trash collection.

details.description: Noes Boat Ramp is located at the end of KY 896 on the upper reach of the Cumberland River above Lake Cumberland. The ramp is located opposite the confluence with Laurel River but, due to low water levels, small boats are recommended. Downstream, small motorized boats can access Lake Cumberland. Upstream, the Cumberland River flows 11.6 miles from the base of Cumberland Falls to Noes and is one of the few whitewater runs that can be made year-round. This section is rated as a Class III with several difficult rapids that should be attempted only by intermediate and advanced paddlers. The last several miles are flat water as the river flows into upper reaches of Lake Cumberland. Plan on 4-6 hours for the trip from the Falls to this boat ramp. The site has parking.

properties.name: WHISTLING ARCH TRAILHEAD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Whistling Arch Trailhead is located along KY 715 in the Red River Gorge and provides access to Whistling Arch Trail #234. The trail leaves the trailhead parking area and extends along a wooded ridge to Whistling Arch. The trail's main attraction is a huge dry rock shelter with a scenic overlook and buttress-type arch formation. The Red River Gorge Geological Area has over 100 natural arches, the greatest concentration of arches east of the Rocky Mountains.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions:
Exit the Mountain Parkway at Slade, KY. Follow KY 11 north 0.1 miles to KY 15. Turn right on KY 15 and travel east 7 miles to KY 715 on left. Turn left onto KY 715 and continue 4.5 miles to the Whistling Arch parking area on the left.
Directions from Pine Ridge: Exit the Mountain Parkway at Pine Ridge (Exit 40) and head west on KY 15 to its junction with KY 715. Turn right on KY 715 and continue 4.5 miles to the Whistling Arch parking area on the left.

properties.name: ALFREY BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Alfrey Boat Ramp is located along Twin Knobs Road just off KY 801 on the eastern shore of Cave Run Lake. Fishing is not allowed from the boat ramp, but once you are in the water, you will find a wide variety of fish species. Cave Run Lake is well-known for excellent muskie fishing. Swimming or sunbathing within 100 feet of any boat launch ramp or courtesy boat dock is prohibited for public safety. The site includes parking, signage, trash collection, security lighting and a courtesy dock.
details.feeDescription:
Day Use:
$5 per day per vehicle
$7 per three day
$50 annual
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. After 8.7 miles, turn right into Twin Knobs. Take the first left (Forest Service Road 1269). The boat ramp is on the left.

properties.name: TAR KILN INTERPRETIVE SITE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Tar Kiln Interpretive Site, which also serves as a popular access point for backcountry camping, is located off Tunnel Ridge Road (#39) in the Red River Gorge. A short interpretive trail leads past historic features of a time when pine pitch was boiled into tar for use as waterproofing, lubricants and cleaners. The site has designated parking, visitor information, trash collection and a picnic table.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: Traveling east on the Mountain Parkway, take exit 33 at Slade. Turn left and then right onto KY 15; go 3 miles and turn left onto Tunnel Ridge Road.

properties.name: LAKEVIEW VISTA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: At Lakeview Vista, nature's beauty unfolds before your eyes. Perched on the edge of a Cave Run Lake, this vantage point offers breathtaking views of Cave Run Lake among the beautiful mountains of eastern Kentucky. This 8,270-acre lake provides flood protection to the lower Licking River valley, supplies water to area communities, improves water flow conditions on the Licking River and offers habitat for many species of fish and wildlife. The site has designated parking and trash collection.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.directions: From I-64, take exit 133 (Farmers Sharkey) and go south on KY 801. At the traffic circle, continue straight to stay on KY 801 S. Continue for 6.5 miles. The site will be on your right.

properties.name: WHITMAN BRANCH SHOOTING RANGE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Whitman Branch Shooting Range is located off Whitman Branch Road (Forest #4055) just west of KY 1193 south of Laurel River Lake Dam. It features five shooting benches with two lanes at 100 yards, one lane at 50 yards and two lanes at 25 yards. Blocks for hanging targets are available at the end of each lane. The site has designated parking, visitor information and trash collection.

details.description: Fishing Point is a popular fishing area is located off of Forest Service Road 611B near the Laurel River Dam. properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
White Sulphur Horse Camp, located near Cave Run Lake, is a primitive campground for horseback riders. The camp provides access to over 50 miles of multiple-use trails winding along forested hills and limestone ridges. Ideal for individual riders and organized groups, the facilities at the horse camp bring riders into the heart of the Daniel Boone National Forest, the Pioneer Weapons Wildlife Management Area, and the Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail #100.
The parking area can accommodate up to 30 vehicles with a trailer up to 50 feet long. Picket lines and a watering trough are available for horses. The campground has no electricity.

The walk is approximately 1/2-mile. Boat moorings are available at the campground for those who boat in. Campsites include tent pads, picnic tables, fire rings and lantern poles. There is no electricity or shower facilities.

properties.name: ZILPO RECREATION AREA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
Zilpo Recreation Area is located at the end of the Zilpo Scenic Byway on a peninsula on the south shore of Cave Run Lake. Zilpo is a prime destination for families. The recreation area includes a large campground, a boat ramp, campground store, a sandy swimming beach, and scenic trails.
The scenic campground offers cabin rentals, tent camping, RV sites with electric hookups, and a selection of lakefront sites. A stand of mixed hardwoods shades the campground, and campsites have good privacy. Each site has a picnic table and campfire ring. Electric hookups are available at some campsites. Bathhouses with showers are spread throughout the campground. An RV dump station is available. Camping cabins sleep up to seven, and have beds, table, porch, accessible ramp entrance and picnic tables.
A campground store with ice, firewood, camping gear and food is on-site. Nearby Zilpo Mountain Trail #1802 leads to an overlook of the lake and Zilpo Connector Trail #113A provides access to many miles of mountain biking and hiking trails.

details.description: Hemlock Grove Picnic Area is located off Rock Creek- Bell Farm Road (Forest #137) in McCreary County and features three double sites, three single sites and a first come, first served group shelter. Rock Creek, a Kentucky Wild River, flows adjacent to the picnic area and is stocked with rainbow trout. The area also serves as a trailhead for a 5-mile loop using Mark Branch Trail #635, Gobblers Arch Trail #636 and Sheltowee Trace National Recreation Trail #100. Along the way, hikers will see Gobblers Arch, a sandstone arch with a height of nearly 12 feet and a base width of 50 feet.
